title: Terry Tao Is on the Front Lines of the Debate Over AI and the Future of Math
source_used: The Indian Express (related coverage of the same debate); the New York Times article itself could not be opened (HTTP 403)
key_facts: [Indian Express] Fields Medallist Terence Tao gave a lecture titled Math 2.0 at Caltech on 9 Oct 2026.
[Indian Express] Tao argued that solving problems is only a means to broader ends in mathematics.
[Indian Express] He said blind optimisation of problem-solving alone is now actively harmful to the long-term health of mathematics.
[Indian Express] He described open problems as lighthouses that guide exploration, not destinations.
[Indian Express] He warned that reaching them too quickly with automated tools risks stifling ideas that emerge along the way.
[Indian Express] The debate sits against AI-made proofs: OpenAI released 722 AI-generated manuscripts on 6 Oct 2026 and three were withdrawn on 7 Oct after a sign error.
[Indian Express] Other researchers urge caution: a formal Lean check does not by itself show a result is mathematically significant.
[NYT headline only] The New York Times says Tao is on the front lines of the debate over AI and the future of math.
quote_evidence: In a lecture at Caltech on October 9, Fields Medallist Terence Tao argued that solving problems, historically one of the most visible goals of mathematical research, is only a means to broader ends.
“Further blind optimization of problem-solving alone is now actively harmful to the long-term health of mathematics,” he said in his presentation titled Math 2.0.
Reaching these problems too quickly through automated tools, he warned, risks disrupting the exploration of alternative approaches and stifling the ideas that might otherwise emerge along the way.
why_it_matters_hint: AI is producing proofs at scale, so mathematicians are rethinking what counts as progress; Tao is a leading voice.
event_date: NYT piece 16 Oct 2026; Tao lecture 9 Oct 2026
